items.title: Christian McBride interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: on the new album I have Chick Corea playing acoustic and electric piano

ctx.x: Yeah the new record is called “Number Two Express” and I’m so excited, I’m so excited, because you know the new album represents me where I am now musically — things I like to listen to and things I like to go for and the things that I would like to eventually have the band get into. You know I’ve always been about diversity. You know you can’t be in just one bag. And I try to make a conscious effort for my band to play you know lots of blues and some progressive stuff maybe some things leaning to a funk, and…

bag so they’ll know what it’s all about. And you know on the new album I have Chick Corea playing acoustic and electric piano and one of the best things about that was him and Jack DeJohnette got to play together again, because Jack is on the album also. And they hadn’t worked together. They told me they’d maybe played together maybe three or four times since 1969. And it was such a thrill for me to have them record on my new CD. And Kenny Garret is on it as well playing alto saxophone. And on the other half of…
Really. You’ve got “Night Train” on there and I said all right, “Night Train.” A classic blues thing. I was wondering, like how is he going to do this? And it’s just bass, right?

items.title: Chick Corea — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Then having Christian there, who is another monster... That synergy took a while.

ctx.x: You had two, maybe three very long tours with that band, and you were together a long time, and I’m sure it was a very different experience at the end than it was at the beginning. I saw it early on, and I saw it later on...

Well, the initial band with John and Kenny Garrett... Kenny Garrett is a monster musician and bandleader and composer, of course, in his own right. So me and John and Kenny, just us getting together, was an interesting way to find how to be on stage together and create together. It happened pretty quickly. Then having Christian there, who is another monster... That synergy took a while. Vinnie was there, holding it all together, and playing great. So it took a while to develop the groupness of it. We started…
It seems almost like a Miles Davis experience, in terms of the music shifting in different directions every night.
